paper_title: On Reduction Probability Models in Lattice Sieving

context: The sphere model is used extensively throughout the lattice sieving literature, because of its simplicity and due to the fact that the mass of an n-dimensional ball concentrates at its boundary as n → ∞. Indeed, this can be observed from the uniform distribution on the n-dimensional ball, which has length PDF f (x) = nxn−1 , that vanishes pointwise for any length x < 1 as n → ∞. However, in practice lattice sieving has been observed to perform better than expected given the sphere model, and it is an open question how this gap behaves asymptotically [AGPS20, ABD+ 21]. Does this gap vanish, or grow as the dimension grows? Our work answers this open question by presenting ball models and showing that the gap is asymptotically constant, with different constants for various cases. Asymptotically, it seems that all radial information is lost from n-dimensional balls, and only the directional distribution is needed. However, analysing the scaled depth w := (1 − x)n, instead of lengths x, one finds that asymptotically the distribution of the scaled depth tends to the exponential distribution Exp(1): n→∞ Pr[w ≥ λ] = Pr[x ≤ 1 − nλ ] = (1 − nλ )n −−−−→ e−λ . (2) This motivates us to look for better models that take the length distribution into account and to compare their advantage with the sphere model.
